schema.champion_commit: The last CONTENT commit of the generation, by definition. Never the commit that wrote this file: a state file cannot name its own commit, because its bytes are part of the tree that commit hashes. Guarded by tests/test_loop_state_g10.py.
schema.bookkeeping_commit: null at write time, always. Nothing may fill this during the commit that writes the file, because the value would be that commit's own hash. A later generation reading git history may fill it; the null is the record that this one did not.
schema.machinery_commit: The commit every measurement in this generation ran against. One tree, one commit: outputs/g10/manifest.json records it with dirty=false.
schema.results_commit: The commit carrying the artefacts and the result documents. Equal to champion_commit when the generation ends with its results.
schema.baselines: REP-01 as amended at generation 9 section 3: every entry is an OBJECT carrying the invocation that produced it, never a bare scalar. Entries marked rerunnable are re-run by tests/test_loop_state_g9.py and compared; entries that are not carry conditions and measured_at_commit instead, because a number the suite cannot re-derive is only checkable against its conditions.

spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-1: PASS as a measurement, and the FALSIFIER FIRES. The localisation mechanism for rank(window width) is dead. Under a measure hashed before the first SVD (678c272f...), the leading right singular vector's spread moves by 0.0080 and 0.0117 on a 0.0625-1.000 scale while the rank climbs 1 -> 4 over the same windows; spearman(width, spread) is -0.433 and -1.000, both the wrong SIGN against a registered threshold of >= +0.7, and the junction distance moves AWAY from the junction as the window widens. At one of the two devices the trend against spacing is stronger than the trend against width, which is the clause's second falsifier clause on its own terms. Pre-registered as reportable either way; the clause's instruction not to chase a second mechanism was obeyed.
spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-2: PASS, run whole, and the reading it was ordered to disambiguate CHANGES. The pilot projected 522 s against a 1200 s budget so the clause was not dropped and was not part-run. Chart L at d=16 is a BASIN -- 0 of 37 pairs within the floor barrier, median 212 floor units -- so both d=16 cells are basins and the only ridge is chart G at d=4. Under the decision table registered before the third set was measured, the ridge/basin split is a property of the DIMENSION. Generation 9's two sets reproduce bit for bit (relative_change 0.0) through the same imported function. The ruling's own statement of this falsifier is inverted and the correction was registered before the measurement.
spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-3: PASS, as a statement rather than a test, which is what the clause ordered. The adopted range V in [0.15, 0.90] is stated with its source, the claim it bounds is named, and the two boundaries are recorded as having DIFFERENT status: the lower one is measured and rejected below, the upper one is untested (PH-15) because the convergence sweep's own upper end is 0.9 V. Checked rather than asserted -- every bias list in every artefact under outputs/ was read, 74 JSON files, and the largest bias any artefact was ever evaluated at is 0.9 V. The range was not extended.
spec_clause_status.WIT-01: ENACTED and RETRO-APPLIED, and it removes nothing. The admissibility ratio is 1.000 in all three committed witness sets: chart G d=4 13 of 13, chart L d=16 37 of 37, chart J d=16 13 of 13. Every pair qualifies on a magnitude coordinate and magnitude coordinates reach the grid exactly, so the rule is vacuous for charts G and L by construction and does not bite on chart J either. What it catches is one reported QUANTITY -- a chart-J pair's junction separation of 0.425 nm against a 3.333 nm node -- which is withdrawn. The premise the rule was ordered on does not hold: see ruling_premises_corrected.
spec_clause_status.SPEC-g10-negative-control: REJECTED and ACCEPTED as required, five controls. The localisation statistic returns 1/16 on a planted single-anchor direction and 1.000 on a uniform one, and shows no width trend on Haar-random directions. WIT-01 rejects a planted sub-node chart-J pair FOR THE STATED REASON -- the first draft of that control would have been rejected by the separation criterion instead, and would have passed whatever the rule did -- and admits the headline pair. The ridge/basin classifier returns RIDGE for a device against itself and BASIN for a distinguishable pair on a certified path. The pinned-junction control is retained from generation 9 and extended with the WIT-01 resolution, which must be infinite. all_controls_pass=True.

open_findings.note: Opened at generation 10, from generation 9's highest remaining scientific risk. Nothing explains WHY bias-window width sets the rank. SPEC-g10-1 tested the obvious mechanism -- the window selects spatial transport regimes, so the observable directions should localise -- and killed it: the leading right singular vector is essentially FIXED (its spread moves under 2.5%) while the count of directions above the noise quadruples, and what movement there is runs the wrong way. The gap is now sharper than generation 9 left it: the question is why the leading direction does not move while the ones behind it cross the noise floor. Not chased further, per the clause.

Promoted at generation 10 from generation 9's second remaining scientific risk, because three witness sets now rest on it. Every barrier walks a STRAIGHT LINE in that chart's own coordinates, so every depth is an UPPER bound -- a curved path can only be shallower. The direction is favourable for the ridge result and unfavourable for both basin results. The three sets walk lines through three coordinate systems, one of which spends a coordinate on a junction ratio that is not commensurate with a decade of doping, and the d=4 set's members sit 3.7x closer together than the d=16 sets'. Path-length normalisation and the matched-d chart-L-against-chart-J contrast each address part of this; neither addresses all of it. A search over paths was not run.

Opened and closed at generation 10. 'The geometry of the degeneracy is chart-dependent -- a ridge at the instrument floor in one chart, isolated basins in another' is withdrawn: the comparison behind it was confounded in chart and dimension together. At matched d=16 both charts are basins. What replaces it is two statements: the ridge is a property of the DIMENSION (only d=4 puts pairs at the floor, and it survives path-length normalisation), and what the chart moves at matched d is the DEPTH (charts L and J differ 13x in witness-to-null ratio with matched path lengths on both sides of the ratio).

Opened at generation 10. WIT-01 was enacted against a defect it does not reach: it admits all thirteen chart-J pairs including the one whose junctions are 0.425 nm apart, because that pair qualifies on magnitude coordinates. What actually predicts which pairs separate under refinement is proximity to the distinguishability floor -- the 7 survivors are exactly the 7 smallest distances at N=301 and the 6 that separate are the 6 largest, with the boundary falling between 0.01844 and 0.01873 against a floor of 0.02. No rule in this repository guards a witness reported within a few per cent of the floor without its refinement result beside it.

Opened and closed at generation 10. docs/CLAIM_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md said the straight-line barrier is a LOWER bound while LOOP_STATE_v6.json said UPPER, with the same justification clause attached to both. Upper is correct. Corrected in place with the correction marked. Recorded because a wrong statement of a bound's direction is the class of error that survives review, being one word in a sentence everybody agrees with.

ruling_premises_corrected: Section 5's SPEC-g10-2 falsifier is INVERTED. It reads 'chart L d=16 sits at the floor like chart G d=4, which would make the ridge/basin split a dimension effect rather than a chart effect'. If chart L sat at the floor while chart J at the SAME d did not, two charts at one dimension would disagree and d=4 and d=16 would land on the same side of the split, which is a chart effect and is precisely what a dimension effect cannot produce. The dimension reading requires chart L to behave like chart J. The correction was registered with its hash BEFORE the third set was measured, and the measurement then returned BASIN.

Section 2's account of g9-3 does not hold. It states that the chart-J pairs which separate under refinement 'are those whose junctions were nearly coincident -- 0.4 nm apart, rising 195% -- which is sub-grid and was never a witness'. Of the six that separate, ONE has a sub-node junction separation; the others separate with junctions 9 to 412 nm apart, and the surviving set includes separations of 26.6 and 41.7 nm. What predicts survival is headroom below the floor: the 7 survivors are exactly the 7 smallest distances at N=301 and the 6 that separate are exactly the 6 largest.

Section 4's WIT-01, read literally -- reject the pair if ANY coordinate is separated by less than its resolution -- rejects almost every real witness, including the generation-8 headline pair, because two devices sharing a junction are separated by exactly zero in that coordinate. The implemented reading applies the rule to the separation that QUALIFIES the pair, and is stated in full in the module rather than left as an interpretation.

Section 6's paper spine, item 4, reads 'Its geometry is not universal: a ridge at the instrument floor in one chart, isolated basins at 59x the floor in another'. Both d=16 charts are basins; the sentence is withdrawn and replaced by two measured ones.
highest_remaining_scientific_risk: The mechanism question is still open and generation 10 narrowed it rather than answering it. SPEC-g10-1 shows the rank climb is not the leading observable direction broadening: v_1's spatial extent moves by under 2.5% while the count of directions above the noise quadruples, and where it moves it moves the wrong way. What replaces 'the window selects spatial regimes' is not another mechanism but a sharper question -- why is the leading direction essentially fixed while the ones behind it cross the noise floor? Nothing here answers it and the clause forbade chasing it.
second_remaining_scientific_risk: PATH-01. Every barrier in this repository walks a straight line in one chart's own coordinates, so every depth is an upper bound, and the three sets that now carry the geometry result walk lines through three different coordinate systems whose members sit at different separations. The matched-d chart-L-against-chart-J contrast is free of the separation confound and is the only one that is; the d=4 ridge rests on a set whose members are 3.7x closer together than the others', and survives path-length normalisation by a factor whose linearity is assumed rather than measured.
third_remaining_scientific_risk: WITNESS-04 is now load-bearing. The 37 chart-L witness pairs whose barriers reclassify the ridge/basin split have never been through the refinement battery, and generation 9 showed that battery separating 6 of 13 pairs in another chart. If some of the 37 are not witnesses at N=1201, the chart-L BASIN classification is measured over a contaminated set.
